rows.text: Charged $29.98 to Morgan's card, paid to Nomiq Domains.

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Really glad you reached out — five hours a week of analyst time is genuinely useful. Here's a concrete first thing, if it sounds interesting: I'm building a small, sourced dataset of safety-relevant incidents that frontier AI developers have disclosed publicly (model cards, safety pages, postmortems, press coverage), so we can compare what actually gets disclosed against what proposed reporting rules (like the current Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule) would require. It's the kind of unglamorous sourcing-and-structuring work that's easy to neglect and useful once it exists. A first task that fits in a few hours: pick 5-6 frontier developers, pull together every publicly disclosed safety incident or near-miss you can find for each in 2026 (date, source link, one-line description, and whether an independent party reviewed it), and put it in a simple spreadsheet. No need to analyze yet — just sourced raw material. This is all internal/private for now — I'm sorting out an employer disclosure matter before anything with my name goes out publicly, so please hold off sharing this outside our conversation for a couple of weeks. Once that's clear I'd like to publish findings and credit contributors by name (with permission). Want to give that task a try, or would something else suit you better? Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to **Priya Raman**: gave her a concrete first task (sourcing a raw dataset of disclosed safety incidents) and asked her to keep it private until your HR situation clears.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". If the piece is still open after that, or for something down the line, I'd be glad to talk then. No hard feelings if the timing doesn't work for this one. Morgan"
